title: 3 Important Reasons to Replace Your Air Conditioner
desc: There are several reasons to replace your air conditioner. Contact Rosenberg Indoor Comfort for your next AC replacement or repair!

blocks.text: So your air conditioner has broken down or simply isn’t running as well as it used to. You’re now faced with that age-old question: is it worth it to repair your air conditioner or should you just buy a new one? Hopefully, this informative guide will help you decide. Here are three reasons you might want to contact Rosenberg Plumbing & Air in San Antonio, TX, to assist you when you need to replace your air conditioner.
1. The AC Is More Than 10 Years Old

Air conditioners generally have a life-span of about fifteen years, assuming you maintain it regularly and keep it in good shape. If your air conditioner is more than ten years old, then it is very likely reaching the end of its useful life, even if you do repair it. In this case, it’s probably more cost-effective just to replace your current AC system by getting a new one. This makes more sense for the long term.
2. Your Air Conditioner Still Uses R-22

R-22 is a refrigerant that is being phased out of use due to new laws aiming to protect Earth’s ozone layer. Modern air conditioner models almost all use R410A, which is not only more environmentally friendly but also more effective. If your AC still uses R-22, it’s good to keep in mind that any repairs that require changing the refrigerant will only continue to get more expensive–as R-22 gets phased out, it will only become harder to find and more pricey. In this case, it might be more convenient (and less expensive in the long run) just to get a new air conditioner.
3. You Want a More Energy-Efficient Model

Modern AC units have been created to use less electricity and cool homes more efficiently. Buying a more efficient AC, in this sense, could save you money in the long run. To find the most energy efficient AC unit, look at the SEER number, or seasonal energy efficiency ratio. The higher the rating, the more energy efficient the unit will be. A SEER of 10 or higher is recommended. Most ACs carry a SEER of between 8 and 21.
